audit_findings.title: Series A preferred is not safely modeled as ordinary dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: $482.0m preferred carrying amount, equal to 5.2% of $9,344m base equity value; 6.775m conversion shares equal to 3.4% of the modeled denominator; 2025 preferred and participating dividends were $34.8m
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes the OE numerator, fully diluted share denominator, and equity bridge depending on whether the preferred remains outstanding, converts, or is redeemed.
audit_findings.evidence: The Series A Senior Preferred Shares rank, with respect to rights as to dividends, distributions, redemptions and payments upon the liquidation, dissolution and winding up of the Company, (a) senior to all of the junior preferred stock, common stock and any other class or series of capital shares of the Company, issued or authorized after the Series A Senior Preferred Shares issuance date, the terms of which do not expressly provide that such class or series ranks senior to or on a parity with the Series A Senior Preferred Shares, (b) on a parity basis with each other class or series of capital shares issued or authorized after the Series A Senior Preferred Shares issuance date, the terms of which expressly provide that such class or series ranks on a parity basis with the Series A Senior Preferred Shares, and (c) junior with each other class or series of capital shares issued or authorized after the Series A Senior Preferred Shares issuance date, the terms of which expressly provide that such class or series ranks on a senior basis to the Series A Senior Preferred Shares.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the instrument is senior and optionally convertible, while the model includes conversion shares without a preferred-claim deduction. Correct direction depends on whether OE is before or after the preferred dividends and allocated earnings. The $482.0m claim and recurring dividends are large enough relative to modeled equity and anchor OE to require explicit alternative cases.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to consolidated income and income available to common holders, then rerun remain-outstanding, conversion, and redemption cases including participating dividends and scheduled rate step-ups.

audit_findings.title: Deferred acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.1m acquisition-date fair value, approximately $0.22 per modeled share and 0.46% of $9,344m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A fixed acquisition-related liability should reduce the equity bridge unless its cash effect is already captured elsewhere; accretion and future-service compensation separately affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The deferred payments that form part of purchase consideration have been recorded as liabilities at their acquisition-date fair value of $ 43.1 million, determined by discounting the contractual payments using the Company’s credit-adjusted discount rate, with $ 13.8 million presented within trade and other liabilities and $ 29.3 million presented within other non-current liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but even deducting the entire filed $43.1m would reduce base value only from $47.31 to approximately $47.09 per share. That scale cannot change the valuation conclusion, although classification and double-counting should still be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 remaining acquisition-consideration liability, deduct that balance from the bridge, and verify that accretion and future-service compensation remain in OE exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The ten-year anchor spans a transformative acquisition perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: The $627.7m anchor is $112.5m, or 15.2%, below 2025 OE of $740.2m; a diagnostic substitution of latest OE would increase base value by approximately $1.58bn or $8.00 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-IAA and post-IAA observations feed the log-trend OE anchor, which then scales forecast OE, operating PV, and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: On March 20, 2023, the Company completed its acquisition of IAA, Inc. (“IAA”) for a total purchase price of approximately $ 6.6 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the fitted series treats the $6.6bn IAA acquisition and its 70.3m issued shares as organic continuation of the earlier business. The resulting anchor difference is large enough to alter the valuation materially. Direction remains unknown because a properly normalized post-IAA OE could be above or below both the current anchor and latest reported OE.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE on a consistent perimeter using post-IAA normalized results or a filed pro-forma splice, then rerun every scenario without changing the stated growth, discount-rate, fade, or margin-of-safety assumptions.

audit_findings.title: All reported cash may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum affected balance is $524.9m, approximately $2.66 per modeled share and 5.6% of $9,344m base equity value; required operating cash is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash after removing its interest income, but any cash required for settlements, advances, seasonal payments, or minimum liquidity is an operating asset rather than distributable excess.
audit_findings.evidence: Our short-term cash requirements include, among others, (i) payment of common share dividends on an as-declared basis and payment of preferential and participating dividends to Series A Senior Preferred Shareholders, (ii) settlement of contracts with consignors, partners and other suppliers, (iii) personnel expenditures, with a majority of short-term incentive compensation paid annually in the first quarter of each fiscal year, (iv) income tax installments, (v) scheduled principal and interest payments on the current portion of long-term debt, (vi) payment of amounts committed under certain service agreements to build our modern IT architecture, (vii) payments on our current operating and finance lease obligations, (viii) other capital expenditures and working capital needs, and (ix) advances.
audit_findings.explanation: The model demonstrably adds the full balance, but the record does not establish how much is surplus. The possible adjustment is large enough to matter to the value estimate, while its actual magnitude cannot be established from the supplied balance alone.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash to restricted funds, auction proceeds payable, book overdrafts, settlement timing, advances, seasonal obligations, taxes, and minimum operating liquidity, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded CRA exposure is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed assessment $55.8m, filed deposit $27.8m, and computed remaining assessed cash amount $28.0m before further interest; exposure for other years is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse resolution would create a cash claim ahead of common equity and may also require correcting OE if related tax, interest, or penalty amounts entered the historical series inconsistently.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 3, 2024, the Canada Revenue Agency (“CRA”) issued the Company a Notice of Assessment and Statement of Interest for C$ 79.1 million ($ 57.8 million), for the taxation years 2010 through 2015, inclusive of C$ 37.7 million ($ 27.5 million) in income taxes, and C$ 41.4 million ($ 30.2 million) in interest and penalties.
audit_findings.explanation: No adverse liability has been established, and management continues to conclude that its position is more likely than not to be sustained. The known assessment alone is small relative to base equity value, but the 2016–2020 exposure and continuing interest are not quantified, so the record cannot establish overall materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current litigation status and a filed or counsel-supported adverse-case estimate for all affected years, net it against the CRA deposit and applicable tax benefits, and scenario-test the resulting common-equity claim.
